$comment: Every rule identifier this toolchain has ever shipped, and what became of it.
Deleting a rule is not a lint-level change for the repos that use it: a flat
config naming a rule the plugin no longer defines makes ESLint exit 2 with
`Could not find "<rule>" in plugin`, and a pre-commit hook id that no longer
exists fails the same way -- the whole repo stops linting before a single file
is read. A stale `eslint-disable` comment is its own error too, because the
So removals and renames are recorded here rather than only in a changelog, and
`code-standards doctor` reads this file to name every stale reference in a
repo BEFORE the upgrade that would break it.
`rules` and `codes` are regenerated by `make sync-rule-ledger`, which never
deletes: an identifier that leaves a registry is moved into `retired`. Fill in
its `note`, and set `status: "renamed"` with a `replacement` when the rule
`kind` is `eslint` for `@sarj/<name>` ESLint rules, `python`/`sql`/`iac` for a
rule id that is also a pre-commit hook id, `text` for config-text rules, and
`code` for a `SARJnnn` code as written in a `sarj-noqa` comment.
